goal: Prove one missing low-risk local capability can be discovered, sandbox-trialed, admitted, executed, persisted, and reused without Provider or network calls.
delivery_approach: adaptive bounded experiment behind stable Foundation contracts
acceptance_criteria: json.parse is absent from the initial registry
offline discovery identifies only the allowlisted Python json.loads candidate
isolated valid, invalid, no-write, no-network, schema, provenance, and effect checks pass
an admission receipt binds the candidate and checks before registry admission
the original DAG node executes after admission
a second process-style registry load reuses the capability without invoking Growth
growth modifies zero kernel files and makes zero Provider or network calls

quality_metrics.actual: PASS; persistent registry loaded and Growth not invoked

quality_metrics.measure: kernel modifications, Provider calls, network calls by Growth

evidence_refs: python -m pytest -q tests/growth tests/capabilities tests/runtime tests/execution tests/state tests/executors
canonical External Executor Discovery for text.slugify returned NOT_EVALUATED with no selected executor and zero trials

feedback: The first run started with json.parse absent, admitted exactly one stdlib candidate, and continued the DAG.
The second run loaded the persisted registry and reused the capability without another Growth invocation.
Self-Growth V1 remains NOT_EVALUATED because canonical discovery produced no candidate with complete ALLOW/PASS/exact-version evidence.

worked: A fixed allowlisted stdlib identity kept V0 deterministic and offline.
Positive admission predicates prevented a false rejection after the first sandbox check exposed inverted boolean semantics.
did_not_work: The initial sandbox receipt represented safety as kernel_files_modified=false and a generic all() treated it as failure.
The optional external search returned incomplete or REVIEW trust evidence and correctly ran no install trial.
experiments: Do not implement V1 admission until canonical discovery can return a complete selected executor for the exact requested package version.
